shots.title: Move publish workflow to npm trusted publishing (#406)

hazards.description: The repo workflow can be corrected, but npm package trusted-publisher settings must be configured on npmjs.com before the failed release can be rerun.

shots.notes: Updated the publish workflow to Node 24, npm 11.5.1+, OIDC trusted publishing without NPM_TOKEN, and documented npm-side maintenance steps.

training.description: npm trusted publishing is split between repo workflow configuration and npm package settings.
training.outcome: The repo now uses OIDC-compatible publishing, but the npm trusted publisher must be configured for package scope authorization.

nutrition.description: Validation used YAML parsing, git diff checks, npm registry version check, and workflow review against npm trusted publishing requirements.

nineteenth_hole.how_did_it_feel: A release-infra fix with one external dependency that cannot be closed from the repository alone.
nineteenth_hole.advice_for_next_player: Before rerunning a failed publish, verify npm trusted publisher settings and then confirm npm view reports the target version.
nineteenth_hole.what_surprised_you: The workflow already had id-token permission, but still used a stale token-based publish path.
nineteenth_hole.excited_about_next: Once npm settings are configured, v1.55.12 can be rerun and future releases should not depend on long-lived tokens.

bunker_locations: GitHub workflow OIDC is necessary but insufficient; npm package settings must authorize the workflow filename and repository.
Node 22 in Actions may carry npm 10, below npm's trusted-publishing CLI requirement.
course_management_notes: Validation used git diff --check and npm view @slope-dev/slope version --registry https://registry.npmjs.org.
npm currently reports @slope-dev/slope latest as 1.55.11; v1.55.12 still needs the publish workflow rerun after npm trusted publisher setup.
